headline: Bridgewater State crash case moves forward as driver held without bail
dek: Steven Mayle, 44, was arraigned on charges including attempted murder after prosecutors said video showed him steering into two students during Homecoming weekend.
body: Steven Mayle, 44, of East Weymouth, was arraigned Monday in Brockton District Court in connection with the Saturday crash that injured two Bridgewater State University students during Homecoming weekend. The Plymouth County District Attorney's Office said Mayle was held without bail and ordered to undergo a further competency evaluation at Bridgewater State Hospital. He is scheduled to return to court Oct. 23 for a dangerousness hearing, according to the office's announcement as reported by the [Fall River Reporter](https://fallriverreporter.com/man-held-without-bail-after-allegedly-striking-two-bridgewater-state-students-authorities-looking-for-driver-in-road-rage-incident-prior-to-crash/).

Prosecutors brought two counts each of attempted murder, assault with intent to murder and leaving the scene of personal injury, along with one count each of reckless operation of a motor vehicle and a marked-lanes violation. Those are allegations, not findings of guilt. The case remains at an early stage, and Mayle is entitled to the presumption of innocence while the court addresses his competency and the Commonwealth's request to keep him in custody.

The underlying incident happened about 10:45 a.m. Saturday on Burrill Avenue near the university's Moakley Center. Two students were taken to area hospitals. Earlier reporting said one had serious but non-life-threatening injuries and the other had minor injuries. The crash occurred as the campus hosted Homecoming activities, a setting that brought a large number of students, families and visitors to the Bridgewater campus.

Assistant District Attorney Samantha Mullin told the court that surveillance video showed Mayle traveling at high speed, turning, jumping a curb and striking both students. [CBS Boston reported](https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/steven-mayle-bridgewater-state-students-struck-suv/) that Mullin described the incident as targeted. That characterization is the prosecution's account of the video and is not a judicial finding. The university previously said there was no evidence the driver had singled out those particular students, a distinction that leaves the alleged deliberate movement of the vehicle separate from any established motive.

Mayle's defense attorney disputed that the act was deliberate or malicious and said his client was experiencing a severe mental-health crisis, CBS Boston reported. A clinician who evaluated Mayle before the arraignment recommended additional evaluation and testified that he appeared unaware of the charges, according to that report. The court's competency process will address whether Mayle can understand the proceedings and assist in his defense; it does not decide whether the collision occurred or whether the criminal charges can ultimately be proved.

Investigators are also examining an alleged road-rage encounter in East Bridgewater that preceded the campus crash. The [Fall River Reporter](https://fallriverreporter.com/man-held-without-bail-after-allegedly-striking-two-bridgewater-state-students-authorities-looking-for-driver-in-road-rage-incident-prior-to-crash/) reported that police are seeking the driver of a white SUV who may have encountered Mayle near a railroad crossing. A witness told police that a man believed to be Mayle approached the SUV and displayed a knife before driving toward Bridgewater. That account remains part of an active investigation, and the SUV driver's version had not been reported.

Bridgewater State, Bridgewater police and East Bridgewater police are investigating the sequence of events. The university's earlier statements said the driver had no affiliation with the school and that the campus police department was coordinating with municipal investigators. The students' names have not been released, and the public reports do not establish a broader threat to the campus or provide a final account of their recovery.

The next confirmed court date is Oct. 23. Until then, the competency evaluation, dangerousness proceedings, additional witness accounts and any later release of evidence are likely to shape the case. The charges describe the seriousness of the alleged conduct, but the final legal outcome will depend on evidence presented in court rather than on the preliminary descriptions from prosecutors, police or news reports.
author: NorthEast News Desk
